pillar: PILLAR A — Knowing Each Other (Love Maps)
name: Personal History & Formative Experiences
objective_questions: Family structure growing up (joint/nuclear/single-parent/other); hometown type (urban/semi-urban/rural).
Number of siblings and birth order.
subjective_questions: What's a childhood experience that still shapes how you see relationships today?
What's one value your family passed down that you don't fully agree with anymore?

pillar: PILLAR A — Knowing Each Other (Love Maps)
name: Daily Life Rhythm & Preferences
objective_questions: Morning/night person; preferred pace of daily life (structured/spontaneous).
Preferred weekend structure (family visits / rest / socializing / religious activities).
subjective_questions: Describe an ordinary Tuesday in the life you actually want — not a vacation, an ordinary day.
What does a fulfilling weekend look like for you, realistically?

pillar: PILLAR A — Knowing Each Other (Love Maps)
name: Fears, Stresses & Coping Triggers
objective_questions: Primary current life stressor category (career/family/health/financial/other).
Comfort asking for help when stressed (Very comfortable / Somewhat / Not at all).
subjective_questions: What's something that quietly stresses you that most people wouldn't guess?
What's a fear about marriage itself, not about your partner, that you rarely say out loud?

pillar: PILLAR A — Knowing Each Other (Love Maps)
name: Dreams, Hopes & Personal Aspirations
subjective_questions: What's a personal dream you have that has nothing to do with marriage or family — just for you?
If money and family expectations were no constraint, what would you actually be doing with your life?

name: Expression of Appreciation
objective_questions: Preferred way to receive appreciation (words / acts of service / gifts / quality time / touch).
Frequency of verbal appreciation expected (Daily / Weekly / Occasionally / Rarely needed).
subjective_questions: Describe the last time someone made you feel truly appreciated — what exactly did they do?
Describe a time you felt taken for granted — what was missing?

name: Respect & Admiration Language
subjective_questions: What's something about a partner you'd want to be able to say out loud, to their face, regularly — what would that actually sound like for you?
What's a quality in your parents' marriage, or another couple you admire, that you hope to have in yours?

name: Conflict Style
objective_questions: Response to conflict (engage immediately / need space first / avoid / escalate then resolve).
Preference for resolving same-day vs. after a cooling-off period.
subjective_questions: Describe the last real disagreement you had with someone close to you — not the topic, but exactly how you handled it, start to finish.
How did your parents model disagreement in front of you, and how did that shape you?

name: Feedback & Criticism Handling
objective_questions: Preferred feedback style (direct/blunt, gentle/indirect, private only, written).
Comfort receiving feedback in front of family or in-laws (Comfortable / Uncomfortable / Depends).
subjective_questions: How do you tend to react in the moment when someone criticizes you — and how do you wish you reacted?

name: Turning Toward / Responsiveness
objective_questions: Expected frequency of daily check-ins (multiple times/day, once/day, as needed).
subjective_questions: When your partner is stressed or excited about something small, what do you want them to do — even if you're busy?
What do you want to still be curious about together with your spouse, 20 years from now?

name: Repair After Conflict
objective_questions: Typical time needed to cool down after conflict (minutes / a few hours / a day or more).
subjective_questions: After a fight, what actually helps you feel okay again — an apology, time, humor, physical affection, something else?

name: Trust Baseline & History
objective_questions: Comfort level trusting a new partner (High / Moderate / Guarded, based on past experience).
Have you discussed past relationships openly with a prospective partner before (Yes / No / Prefer not to)?
subjective_questions: What would break your trust in a way you don't think you could fully rebuild?
What would you need to hear from a partner to trust them with something painful from your past?

name: Commitment Philosophy
objective_questions: View on divorce as an option (Only in extreme circumstances / A reasonable option if unhappy / Should never be considered).
Openness to couples therapy if things get hard (Open to it / Only as last resort / Not for us).
subjective_questions: What does 'for better or worse' actually mean to you in practice — where's the line, if there is one?

name: Temperament & Stress Processing
objective_questions: Self-described temperament (calm/steady, expressive/emotional, reserved/private, variable).
Typical response under social/family pressure — criticism from elders, public gatherings (Withdraw / Push back / Deflect with humor / Stay composed).
subjective_questions: What's something about your temperament that people who know you well would warn a future spouse about — the honest version.

name: Emotional Regulation
objective_questions: Preference when upset — being left alone vs. being comforted.
subjective_questions: When you're upset, how long does it typically take you to be ready to talk about it — and what do you need in that window?

name: Personal Boundaries & Autonomy Needs
objective_questions: Personal space needs (High / Moderate / Low).
Comfort with partner taking solo trips or vacations without you (Comfortable / Occasional / Rare / Not comfortable).
subjective_questions: What does personal space and independence look like for you inside a marriage — hobbies, friendships, time alone?

name: Comfort with Vulnerability
subjective_questions: How easily do you show a partner when you're struggling, versus needing to appear fine?
Who was the first person you ever told something you were ashamed of — what made that possible?

pillar: PILLAR F — Family of Origin & Extended Family (India-critical)
name: Family of Origin Dynamics
objective_questions: Was your household hierarchical (elders decide) or egalitarian growing up?
subjective_questions: How were disagreements handled in your parents' marriage — and how much of that do you want to repeat or avoid?

pillar: PILLAR F — Family of Origin & Extended Family (India-critical)
name: In-Law Relationship Expectations
objective_questions: Expected interaction frequency with in-laws if living separately (Daily / Weekly / Occasional / Minimal).
Would you expect a spouse to observe specific traditional deference toward elders (touching feet, specific forms of address, etc.)?
subjective_questions: How much say should parents/in-laws have in decisions after marriage? Give a specific example where you'd want their input, and one where you wouldn't. / If your spouse and your parent were in conflict over something involving you, how do you think you'd actually handle it?
Describe an in-law conflict you've witnessed in a friend's or relative's marriage — what would you do differently?

pillar: PILLAR F — Family of Origin & Extended Family (India-critical)
name: Parental Involvement in Major Decisions
objective_questions: Should parents be told when you and your spouse have a serious fight (Never / Only if serious / Openly, as a norm)?
subjective_questions: Describe a decision you'd want your parents involved in after marriage, and one you'd consider entirely off-limits to them.

pillar: PILLAR F — Family of Origin & Extended Family (India-critical)
name: Sibling & Extended Kin Obligations
objective_questions: Financial/caregiving obligations to extended family currently or expected (Yes, ongoing / Possible future / None expected).
Do you expect to financially support siblings' education or marriage costs in the future?
subjective_questions: Are there extended-family obligations — financial or caregiving — that a partner should know about upfront?

name: Living Arrangement Preference
objective_questions: Joint family / nuclear same city / nuclear different city / flexible.
If joint family, whose parents — yours, partner's, either, neither?
subjective_questions: Describe the household you imagine living in 5 years from now — who's in it, who decides what, how money and space are shared.

name: Gender Roles & Division of Labor
objective_questions: Who primarily manages chores/finances/childcare/elder care.
Who should manage the household budget day-to-day?
Who made major decisions in your family growing up (mother / father / joint / other)?
subjective_questions: What does an equal partnership look like to you, practically — who does what, and why? / What would you want a partner to never expect of you, and what would you happily take on unasked?
Describe a decision you'd want full control over, and one you'd want to make only together, no matter what.

name: Post-Marriage Career Continuity & Autonomy
objective_questions: Expectation if working at time of marriage (continue with full support / continue but will need to negotiate / expected to stop / open, decide together) — asked of and about both parties.
Would you relocate cities for your partner's career, and would you expect them to relocate for yours?
Centrality of professional ambition to identity (1–5 scale).
subjective_questions: If your career and your partner's family's expectations came into direct conflict, how do you think that would actually get resolved in your household — not how it should, how it would.
If your partner's career required real sacrifice from you for a few years, how would you actually think about that — not the ideal answer, the honest one?

name: Elder Care Responsibility
objective_questions: Expectation for caring for aging parents (Yours / Partner's / Both / Will hire help / Undecided).
If elder care requires one partner to pause a career temporarily, whose job takes priority by default?
subjective_questions: How do you picture caring for aging parents — yours or your spouse's — practically, not just in principle?

name: Financial Philosophy
objective_questions: Saver vs. spender self-rating (1–5).
Do you currently have any debt or loans a partner should know about?
subjective_questions: Is money something you save toward a number, or spend toward a life? Explain how you actually think about it.

name: Financial Structure & Control
objective_questions: Preferred account structure (joint/shared control, joint/one manages, separate, hybrid).
Should both partners have full visibility into each other's individual accounts, even if kept separate?

name: Marriage-Onset Financial Transparency
objective_questions: Financial expectations around the wedding — gifts, contributions, dowry-adjacent practices a partner should know upfront (Yes, will disclose / No / Prefer to discuss privately) — flagged for private disclosure during matched conversation, never scored publicly.
subjective_questions: What financial expectations, spoken or unspoken, exist in your family around marriage — and how do you personally feel about them?

name: Major Purchase & Debt Comfort
objective_questions: Threshold amount above which you'd always consult your partner before spending (e.g. under ₹10k / ₹10k–50k / ₹50k–1L / above ₹1L).
subjective_questions: Describe a financial decision you'd never make without discussing first, and one you'd never need to discuss at all.

name: Physical & Intimate Compatibility
objective_questions: Importance of daily physical affection (1–5); comfort discussing intimacy expectations pre-marriage.
Comfort discussing intimacy-adjacent health topics (fertility, STIs) openly before marriage.

name: Affection Expression Style
subjective_questions: What does affection look like for you in daily life — not just intimacy, but touch, closeness, attention?
What's a small daily gesture, not intimacy, that would make you feel loved?

name: Desire for Children & Timing
objective_questions: Want children (Yes/No/Undecided/Open to partner's strong preference); rough timeline preference.
If unable to conceive naturally, openness to adoption, IVF, or surrogacy.

name: Parenting Philosophy & Discipline
objective_questions: Approach (strict/discipline-focused, balanced, permissive, undecided).
Should children be raised bilingual/multilingual — regional mother tongue plus English?
subjective_questions: What kind of childhood do you want to give your children — describe the household culture, not just 'good values' as a phrase.

name: Education & Upbringing Values
objective_questions: Comfort with children pursuing non-traditional careers (arts, sports, startups) vs. conventional paths (engineering, medicine, government service).
subjective_questions: How much academic/career pressure do you think is right to put on a child — and where did that view come from?

pillar: PILLAR K — Social Life, Community & Habits
name: Friendship Boundaries
objective_questions: Comfort with partner's opposite-sex friendships (fully comfortable / comfortable with transparency / prefer minimal / not comfortable).
Comfort with a partner having close opposite-sex friends from before the marriage specifically.

pillar: PILLAR K — Social Life, Community & Habits
name: Social & Community Involvement
objective_questions: Preferred social pace (frequent socializing / occasional / minimal, prefer close circle).
Importance of maintaining your own independent friend circle post-marriage (1–5).

pillar: PILLAR K — Social Life, Community & Habits
name: Lifestyle Habits & Health
objective_questions: Diet type; alcohol/smoking/substance use (self and expectation of partner); activity level.
Attitude toward non-vegetarian food or alcohol being present at home, even if you personally don't partake.
subjective_questions: How would you feel if your partner's health habits were meaningfully different from yours? Where's your real line, versus what you'd adjust to?

name: Spiritual Practice Intensity
objective_questions: Practice centrality (1–5); frequency (Daily/Weekly/Occasional/Festivals only/Rarely).
Would you want a partner to join you in religious rituals or festivals even if they're not equally devout?
subjective_questions: Describe what your faith actually looks like day to day — not what you were raised with, but what you currently practice and believe. / If your partner's spiritual intensity were noticeably different from yours, what would that change about daily life together?

name: Philosophical Orientation on Meaning
subjective_questions: Where do you turn, practically, when life feels meaningless or hard — faith, philosophy, people, work, something else?
Has your relationship with faith changed since childhood — how, and why?

pillar: PILLAR M — Shared Meaning & Long-Term Vision
name: Shared Rituals & Traditions
objective_questions: Which festivals matter most to you, and how do you expect to celebrate them post-marriage — your family's style, partner's, or blended?
subjective_questions: What family or personal traditions do you want to carry into your own household — and which ones would you deliberately leave behind?

pillar: PILLAR M — Shared Meaning & Long-Term Vision
name: Long-Term Life Vision
objective_questions: Openness to living in a different city or abroad, even temporarily.
subjective_questions: Where do you see your life in 10 years — city, work, family shape, lifestyle?

pillar: PILLAR M — Shared Meaning & Long-Term Vision
name: Life Purpose & Meaning of Marriage
subjective_questions: In your own words, what is marriage for? What does it accomplish that living together without it wouldn't? / What would make you consider your marriage a success 30 years from now — even on days it wasn't 'happy'? / What's a life you'd actively refuse to live, even for love?

name: Caste & Community Preference
objective_questions: Do you have a caste/community preference or restriction? (No preference / Same caste preferred / Same caste required / Other).
